metadataReview.note: Sierra Maestra, the provincial newspaper of Santiago de Cuba, states that General José Maceo was gravely wounded in the battle of Loma del Gato on 5 July 1896 and died hours later at La Soledad de Ti Arriba, near Songo-La Maya, and refers to the obelisk at Loma del Gato marking where he fell. The atlas point is the gazetteer node for the Loma del Gato hamlet in Songo-La Maya. It is a named-place sector reference, not the spot where Maceo fell, a Spanish or Cuban position, or the extent of the action. The existing date is retained. Strengths, losses and equipment are not inferred.

metadataReview.coordinateBasis: Nominatim lookup of OpenStreetMap node 5873644189 (place=hamlet, name Loma del Gato, municipality Songo - La Maya) returns latitude 20.1252947 and longitude -75.6857666, rounded to [-75.6858,20.1253]. A separately mapped monument to José Maceo lies about 400 m to the west-south-west and is not used. A 1077 m peak also named Loma del Gato west of Santiago de Cuba is rejected because the source places Maceo's death hours later near Songo-La Maya. This is a named-hamlet reference, not a surveyed combat position; no accuracy radius is claimed.
